subject: castle-towers-v5
label: Straight-on corner towers for the back-left and back-right of the courtyard
notes: THE GAP THIS FILLS. Raheem, 2026-08-07: 'the back left and right towers, we literally don't have any because the examples we have are tilted forty five degrees to the left or right. We kinda just need straight up and down towers.' Verified: castle-tower-aegis/beacon/gatewatch/starward-healthy are ALL isometric AND in the old warm cream sandstone palette, and the wall-corner-inner-v2 / -outer-v2 / -turn pieces are isometric corner views. The ONLY straight-on tower in the kit is castle-tower-watch-v2, which is placed three times already. So the back corners have no usable art.

PIXELLAB, NOT LEONARDO, AND THE REASON IS FUNCTIONAL. Raheem: 'we can't use the Lucid engine over Pixel Lab because all the rest of the castle is generated in Pixel Lab, and we need it to crack with the rest of the castle. We need it to be an actor.' The castle is a damageable surface, not a backdrop. A Leonardo tower could match on palette and still be the one piece that cannot take a crack.

PALETTE IS STATED IN THE PROMPT AND THEN LEFT ALONE. Carried forward from castle-walls-v4: 'forcing a palette onto art that is already right washes it out and killed the gold. Logged twice now.' Confirmed a third time on 2026-08-07 during the forge work, where a ramp_transfer against a white-backed reference washed the plate pale and turned the furnace fire white. Do NOT ramp_transfer these.

THE PALETTE NAMES ARE CORRECTED FROM v4. v4's notes describe 'honey-gold sandstone rgb(214,184,145)' — that is the OLD kit. Measured 2026-08-07 from the assets actually in CourtyardV2: mid stone rgb(174,157,171) / rgb(166,149,157) pale violet-grey; shadow stone rgb(117,98,121) / rgb(105,85,108) deep violet; highlight rgb(221,209,203) / rgb(213,193,181) warm cream-white; trim rgb(230,160,38) which is a BRIGHT SATURATED AMBER, not a pale sandstone. Outline is pure rgb(0,0,0). Calling the trim 'honey sandstone' is what would drift these away from the castle.
DATUM UNCHANGED from castle-walls-v4: tile 32px, tower 288x384 (9x12 tiles). Whole tiles so pieces snap without nudging.

VIEW IS 'side', THE SAME AS THE SOUTH WALL AND THE GATE. These are corner towers read face-on from the courtyard, so they are ELEVATION. The wall runs going away from the camera are 'low top-down'; towers are not. Getting this wrong is what produced the isometric batch already sitting in structures/towers.

NO STYLE REFERENCE ON PURPOSE. /create-1-direction-object refuses `size` whenever `style_images` is supplied, which is what produced the 88px rug set that went blurry when scaled up. The `images` path used by castle-walls-v4 takes no reference and honours image_size, which is why the v2 walls are full size and on-palette. Angle and palette are held by the prompt instead.

NO BAKED BACKGROUNDS. Every prompt says standing alone against transparency. Two v3 pieces came back with a drawn background and enclosed regions behind merlons cannot be reached by an edge flood-fill.

images.note: Back-left. Round drum tower — reads clearly different from the square watch tower already placed three times.
